topic: How should the skill advisor surface slash commands (all 45 under .skilled/commands, not only /doctor) so a model either runs the matching command workflow by itself or asks the user first, and how does a request typed as plain chat with no slash command still reach the proper command workflow on every runtime? Work through the ten research angles in section 3 of specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/007-command-surfacing-and-workflow-enforcement/spec.md: inventory, scoring, output contract, run or ask, invocation mechanics, chat-only users, skill and command linkage, measurement, prior art, failure modes. Start from the advisor runtime in .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor (command-bridges, scorer projection and fusion, render.ts), the commands tree, AGENTS.md gates 2 and 4, and the prior packets 003-doctor-command-surfacing and system-speckit/spec-authoring-and-continuity/005-goldfish-cold-read-plan-review. Cite path:line for every claim and name evidence that contradicts a recommendation as well as evidence that supports it.

focus: Angle 1 inventory: commands tree vs bridge inventory in both directions, per-runtime enablement, and the one runnable-string path in render.ts
Angle 2 scoring: command projection population, lane weights, slash-only command keywords, plain-phrase boost coverage and the read-only/mutating confidence cliff
answeredQuestions: Why do plain planning and research prompts return zero recommendations, and what do the no-slash penalty and the mutating-command gate cost in recall versus what they buy in precision?

focus: Angle 3 output contract: public strict schema, both brief sentence forms, doctor-only runnable labelling, and the real token budget of the emitted brief
answeredQuestions: What must the advisor_recommend output contract carry (kind, runnable, brief wording, token budget) for a model to act on a surfaced command instead of a raw bridge id?

focus: Angle 4 run-or-ask: frontmatter write capability, the 25 [:auto|:confirm] hints, doctor mutating taxonomy (15 read-only / 2 add-only / 18 mutates), and the existing blast-radius ladder as the policy vocabulary
answeredQuestions: Which commands are safe to start without asking, which need a question first, and where should that run-or-ask policy live?

focus: Angle 5 invocation mechanics: per-runtime command mirrors, seven brief adapters versus a six-row doc table, and the two universal fallbacks (name-and-ask, load-and-follow)
answeredQuestions: Can a model start a slash command by itself on Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Cursor, Devin and DSH, and what fallback exists where it cannot?

focus: Angle 6 chat-only users: brief advisory contract, AGENTS.md as sole root doc and binding surface, 1-of-14 skill command pointers, runner refusal limits, and the three-layer mechanism
answeredQuestions: Which mechanism actually brings a plain-chat request onto the command workflow on every runtime: advisor brief, AGENTS.md gate, hook, skill-to-command pointer, or runner refusal?

focus: Angle 7 skill and command linkage: three incompatible linkage carriers, 18 of 19 ownerMode resolutions, create/agent and speckit/plan routers that bypass skills, and why skill-to-command implication is unsound
answeredQuestions: Which command workflows never load the mode SKILL.md their metadata names, and should a skill recommendation imply its command?

focus: Angle 8 measurement: four corpora, doctor-only command expectations (17 of 35 bridges covered), chat-style share of 63 of 78 rows, 19 control rows, and the missing command-level metrics
answeredQuestions: Which benchmark rows and metrics separate a missed command from a wrongly started one?

focus: Angle 9 prior art from the shipped runtime mirrors: three-surface convergence, a static Cursor routing rule whose dynamic adapter is dormant, Devin inheritance, and the generated-fence anti-drift pattern
answeredQuestions: What prior art exists for routing free text to a packaged workflow, and which failure modes (over-trigger, command/skill ambiguity, child sessions starting commands, loops, brief budget) must a design guard against?

focus: Angle 10 failure modes: ungated child sessions in the advisor path, existing over-trigger and default_target guards, the brief-command-advisor cycle, budget headroom, dormant delivery, and ownerMode dead references
answeredQuestions: What prior art exists for routing free text to a packaged workflow, and which failure modes (over-trigger, command/skill ambiguity, child sessions starting commands, loops, brief budget) must a design guard against?
